articles.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
articles.source: BBC News
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during a 2017 military crackdown.
articles.explain: The ICJ is the highest UN court for settling disputes between countries. Genocide is defined as the deliberate killing or destruction of a large group of people, especially those of a particular ethnic group or nation. This ruling is historic as it is the first time in the ICJ's 80-year history that the court has officially determined that a state committed the act of genocide, which carries immense legal and moral weight globally.

story.title: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Rohingya Genocide
story.so_far: In 2017, Myanmar's military launched a violent crackdown on the Rohingya, a Muslim ethnic minority in Rakhine State, leading to the deaths of thousands and the exodus of nearly a million refugees to Bangladesh. The small West African nation of Gambia filed a case against Myanmar at the ICJ in 2019, accusing the country of violating the 1948 Genocide Convention.

timeline.text: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during a 2017 military crackdown.
The court's judges delivered a final verdict officially labeling Myanmar's actions as genocide.
The verdict concludes a seven-year judicial process and provides a legal determination on the 2017 atrocities.

articles.title: Wrapped Monero token plunges 99% as issuer-linked wallet sells $13.5 million
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: The value of a 'wrapped' Monero token crashed by 99% following a large sale from a wallet linked to its issuer.
articles.explain: A 'wrapped' token is essentially a digital receipt that allows you to use a cryptocurrency on a network where it doesn't normally function. If the issuer of that receipt sells off their reserves or loses control, the link to the original asset breaks, causing the token's value to plummet.

story.title: Wrapped Token Market Volatility
story.so_far: Wrapped tokens are tokens on one blockchain (like Ethereum) that are meant to represent the value of a token on a different blockchain (like Monero). They rely on 'bridges' or custodial services to maintain a 1:1 value ratio, making them susceptible to technical failures, mismanagement, or fraud.

timeline.text: A $13.5 million sell-off by an issuer-linked wallet triggered a nearly total collapse in the price of the wrapped Monero token.
